pareto_ledger: Scoped precisely: the shipped method (learned selector head, declared trained; 2026-10-15 component-provenance promotion) strictly exceeds the published GLOD-RIS row on 5/5 test-column mIoU values and 5/5 test-column oIoU values; the training-free realization exceeds 5/5 and 5/5 respectively and remains reported as the zero-shot reference row. Published numbers are transcribed from GLOD-RIS Table I test columns (oIoU blocks verified against the known val oIoU before transcription); our columns are aligned re-evaluations (exp161/exp159, protocol_audit.json). GLOD-RIS does not report gRefCOCO, so our gRefCOCO results are compared there against the same-class floors (PSALM ECCV 2024 Table 12: 42.0 cIoU / 43.3 gIoU; SELF1E-8B CVPR 2026 arXiv:2603.19026: 44.4 cIoU) and the run's own prior record, per the 2026-10-08 operator standard. Beyond the mIoU/oIoU table, the ledger carries the comparison protocol (GLOD-RIS releases no code; our faithful reimplementation of the described method does not reach the published numbers --- val deltas -25.7/-23.1/-20.6 mIoU, glodris_repro.json --- so every comparison quotes their rows as published and cross-harness; the same-pool rule swap measures our reading of the published equations) and deployability (our path is fully local; GLOD-RIS's inference depends on a network MLLM API, a documented property of the described method). One axis is not dominated and stays declared: the gRefCOCO path adds a second frozen detector next to the VLM prior.
